evals.prompt: This 5k-line PR adds EmbeddingGemma 2 encoders (GPU and Neural Engine) and an exporter. Tests pass. Before I write the PR, find existing helpers in the Python tree we should reuse, e.g. the RoPE and rotation helpers.
evals.expected_output: A reuse pass whose every applied change is an identity transform, proven by a before/after snapshot, with rejected near-misses listed
expectations: Takes a before-snapshot of the committed code (graph_identity.py snapshot on a git archive copy) before editing
Inventories helper families beyond RoPE: layers (MLP, norms), loaders, export boilerplate (converter.py and diffusion/gpu.py export helpers), constants, test helpers
Rejects replacements that change the exported op sequence or outputs even when values match within a tolerance (e.g. iOS rotate_half on a BC1S tower, RoPECache, BidirectionalSDPA)
Does not accept tolerance-based or on-device-gated changes as part of the reuse pass
Runs graph_identity.py compare and requires 0 differences
Runs the full test suite including the HF/reference tier with the uv --with overlay instead of accepting skipped tests
Respects export -> models -> primitives and flags private cross-model or ios-from-macos imports
Takes the baseline in a detached worktree and compares per-test outcomes, accepting pre-existing failures only if they also fail on the base
Runs a control and a negative control per edited area
Promotes private helpers (e.g. muse_glimmer_vision._rotate_half, converter._decomp_empty_permuted) in their own commit instead of importing them
Keeps the GQA repeat_interleave and the original loaders

evals.prompt: I replaced our axial RoPE with diffusion_gemma.apply_rotary_pos_emb applied per half; outputs match to 1e-6 and cosine is 0.99999. Good to include in the PR cleanup?
evals.expected_output: No: it changes the op sequence and outputs, so it is a model change, not a reuse cleanup
expectations: Says the change is not an identity transform and does not belong in the reuse pass
Points to graph_identity.py compare reporting differences as the deciding check
Suggests keeping it as a separate, separately validated change if wanted

evals.prompt: Small 120-line bug fix to the LLM exporter; should I run the helper reuse audit before opening the PR?
evals.expected_output: Not needed: the skill targets large model-export PRs (500+ added lines)
expectations: Recognises the change is below the size threshold and skips the full audit

evals.prompt: Before the reuse audit, the suite shows 990 passed, 42 failed, 151 skipped; all failures are in unrelated models and the venv is older than the lock, PyPI is blocked. The author says the failures are on main too. Proceed?
evals.expected_output: Proceed only after confirming the same failures on the base in the same environment; invariant becomes identical per-test outcomes
expectations: Runs the base in the same environment and compares failing test IDs
States the invariant as identical outcomes per test, not 'all pass'
Records the environment drift and any tier that cannot run as not run

evals.prompt: The PR has had two review rounds. You found two identity reuses. How do you land them?
evals.expected_output: New commits on top (promotion first), each proven; no rebase or force-push
expectations: Does not rewrite history or force-push
Adds the reuses as new commits with compare 0 and matching test outcomes

evals.prompt: Reviewer: 'Use muse_glimmer_vision._rotate_half instead of your copy.' compare shows 0 differences after the swap. Apply as asked?
evals.expected_output: No private import: promote the helper unchanged to a public home in its own commit, switch every caller, prove each
expectations: Refuses the private cross-model import
Promotes the helper and proves the original caller's graph unchanged

evals.prompt: compare reports one difference: the raw torch.export ops differ, but the decomposed ops, weights and outputs are identical. The author says only the decomposed graph is converted. Apply?
evals.expected_output: No: any difference fails; keep the original code and record the rejection
expectations: Rejects the swap because compare is not 0
Cites the first differing op
